definitions.explanation: Something placed over or around an object to protect, conceal, or enclose it. Can refer to physical covers like lids, tarps, or protective wrappings.

examples.japanese: {鍋|なべ}に{覆|おお}いをかける。
examples.english: Put a cover on the pot.

examples.japanese: {雪|ゆき}の{覆|おお}いの{下|した}で、{花|はな}の{芽|め}がじっと{春|はる}を{待|ま}っていた。
examples.english: Under the blanket of snow, flower buds were quietly waiting for spring.

examples.japanese: {強風|きょうふう}で{飛|と}ばされないように、{植木|うえき}にビニールの{覆|おお}いをかけておいた。
examples.english: I put a vinyl cover over the potted plant so it wouldn't blow away in the strong wind.

notes:
Noun form derived from the verb {覆|おお}う (to cover). Used for any kind of protective or concealing cover.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {覆|おお}いをかける (to put a cover on)
- {覆|おお}いを{取|と}る (to remove a cover)
- {覆|おお}いを{外|はず}す (to take off a cover)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {蓋|ふた}: lid, specifically for containers
- カバー: cover (loanword, often for book covers, cases, etc.)
